sanskrit_verse: प्रदद्यात् त्वेव पिण्डं वा क्षेत्रांशं वा यदृच्छया //
transliteration: pradadyāt tveva piṇḍaṃ vā kṣetrāṃśaṃ vā yadṛcchayā
sph_interpretive_translation: One must unconditionally give food or land when requested, without expectation or condition.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the capacity to give without attachment
Causation arises from the alignment of abundance and need
Capacity-based responsibility demands response to genuine scarcity
Restoration logic operates through voluntary resource circulation
Consciousness alignment manifests via detachment from ownership
executable_legal_axioms: IF a being requests sustenance AND requester lacks access THEN provider with surplus MUST transfer resource
IF land is held beyond necessity THEN holder MUST allocate portion upon spontaneous request
NO conditional clause SHALL invalidate gratuitous giving
AUTOMATED DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM shall prioritize requests aligned with biological necessity
OWNERSHIP VALIDITY decreases proportionally with hoarding duration
supreme_court_application: In adjudication concerning property rights, the threshold of legitimate possession is measured not by title alone but by responsiveness to collective sustenance needs. Hoarded resources become legally obsolete if they remain unshared during known societal deficit.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that withholding necessary resources creates causal imbalance. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how accumulated scarcity leads to systemic collapse. Responsibility lies with those whose capacity exceeds their responsive action. Dharma restores equilibrium through conscious redistribution rather than punitive seizure.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Provider undergoes guided practice of generosity until natural abundance flows
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Holder acknowledges role in creating artificial scarcity
Capacity Restoration: Individual reconnects with innate sense of sufficiency
Integrity Reintegration: Community facilitates transparent sharing systems
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Giving without condition is the highest Dharma. There is no punishment where there is no retention. Consciousness itself adjudicates truth.
